function: Excluded (above_phy): learning acts only on UAV placement (N1-step dueling DDQN, pp. 7, 10) and user selection (ANN predicting gradient changes, p. 7); bandwidth allocation is convex optimization (p. 9).
notes: Title and DOI match on p. 1. The learned parts of the method act above the physical layer. UAV placement by DRL, p. 7: "In the outer layer algorithm, the DRL method is utilized to optimize the deployment location of the UAV"; p. 10: "the action space A corresponds to the UAV deployment direction an which includes four directions". User selection (scheduling) by an ANN, p. 7: "we utilize an ANN neural network to predict it, so as to determine the probability of unselected users selection". The only physical-layer decision is not learned, p. 9: "(P3) is a convex optimization problem, which can be solved utilizing convex optimization toolbox technology such as CVX"; p. 8: "the transmission power Pl and PD are constant". So the aerial-link exception (learned power, resource allocation or beams) does not apply. FL aggregates digitally, not over the air (p. 5: OFDMA uplink of model parameters; p. 8: "each selected user occupies an individual resource block"), so not area 7. The FL-trained radio map is the application served by the links, not the proposed method, pp. 12-13: "our proposed method does not rely on a particular radio map model". Reviewer check: a literal reading of no_learning (the only physical-layer decision, bandwidth, is classical) would also exclude; above_phy was chosen because the method itself contains learning, and that learning targets UAV placement and user selection, both listed under above_phy.
